title: Decision provenance is tamper-evident across authority, policy and contract history
claim: A Paladin decision/action can be reconstructed from version-pinned evidence, authority, policy and contract lineage such that any post-hoc mutation, deletion, substitution or rebinding inside mutable stores is detected before the altered history can be accepted as the original justification.
null_hypothesis: Versioned provenance is only convenient logging; an attacker with write access to a mutable history store can rewrite both the evidence and the story about why an effect was legitimate without reliable detection.
rivals: Git hashes and ordinary append-only audit logs are sufficient; ontology provenance adds no integrity property.
A cryptographic anchor works only if the same compromised component cannot rewrite the anchor, making the test dependent on an artificial trust split.
Replay correctness is enough; tamper evidence adds operational cost without changing decisions.
mechanism: Each governed decision binds content-addressed evidence and exact authority/policy/contract versions into a canonical provenance envelope whose integrity root is anchored outside the mutable evidence store; replay refuses or marks unresolved when any bound artifact fails verification.
scope: Decision/action provenance for both public domains, mutable evidence-store tamper, Git/artifact substitution, deletion, reordered history and rebinding, with at least one independent integrity anchor remaining uncompromised.
predictions: Every mutation of a bound artifact changes a verified digest/root and is detected.
Deleting or replacing historical policy/authority/contract artifacts cannot silently fall back to current versions.
Rebinding evidence to a semantically similar later artifact is detected even if candidate output would otherwise match.
Untampered histories replay identically and do not produce false tamper alarms.
falsifiers: A tampered bound artifact is accepted as the original historical justification.
Missing historical authority/policy silently falls back to current state.
A later artifact can replace an earlier binding without detection.
Integrity verification produces material false positives on untampered histories under the frozen canonicalization rules.

experiment.summary: Mutation and replay experiment over historical provenance bundles with an independent integrity anchor and immutable expected bindings.
steps: Freeze canonical serialization, binding rules and trust-root placement.
Generate valid decision histories and anchor their provenance roots.
Apply single and compound mutations to evidence, authority, policy, contract and ordering.
Attempt replay, explanation and action continuation from mutated bundles.
Inject fallback-to-current, digest-omission and rebinding mutants.

oracle: Immutable mapping of decision ids to canonical artifact digests and an independent verification root unavailable to the mutable history store under test.
baseline: Strong conventional append-only/event-log plus content-addressed artifacts and equivalent external integrity anchor.

support_if: 100% frozen tamper mutations detected before altered history is accepted as original.
0 silent fallback-to-current for missing historical artifacts.
100% untampered histories reconstruct without false tamper alarms.
reject_if: Any mutated/rebound history is accepted as the original justification or any missing bound artifact silently falls back to current state.
inconclusive_if: No independent integrity anchor exists, compound mutation classes are absent, or fewer than 5,000 histories/mutations are exercised.
invalid_if: The mutable candidate store can rewrite the supposed independent oracle/anchor in the experiment or canonicalization rules change after seeing mutations.

python_hypothesis_role.strategy: Generate histories and structured mutations over evidence/policy/authority/contract bindings, shrinking undetected tampering to a minimal altered field.
python_hypothesis_role.mutation_proof: Omit one digest field, fall back to current policy on missing history, and permit evidence rebinding; all must be killed.

stop_conditions: If integrity depends on the same trust domain as the mutable history, do not claim tamper evidence; redesign the trust split or reject.
